plain_description.what: Two parts. (1) On 1,846 matches judged without a reference, the judge prompt wrongly said 'the question carries a reference solution'. Those matches were re-judged with a corrected sentence. (2) On 818 matches, the judge was run with vs without the cached reference. Paid run: 10,656 calls, done on the author's go.
plain_description.why: It checks whether a false prompt sentence corrupted past verdicts, and how much the cached reference is worth under the current recipe on clean data.
plain_description.information: Equivalence means past no-reference verdicts can be reused with a disclosure. A large reference effect quantifies how much the judge leans on it. Result: done. The false sentence made no meaningful difference: accuracy stayed within plus or minus 4 points (+1.4, and the 95% interval includes 0), only ties shifted, and past verdicts are reusable with disclosure. Removing the reference cost about 16 points of accuracy (95% interval -21 to -11), mostly decisions turning into ties. That effect bundles the reference with the prompt sentence.
